newsitem.title: USA: Phillips sets deep North Cook Inlet drilling.
newsitem.headline: Phillips sets deep North Cook Inlet drilling.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said an agreement reached with Atlantic Richfield Co clears the way for additional delineation drilling in the deep oil zone beneath the Phillips-operated Tyonek production platform in Alaska's North Cook Inlet.
Under the deal, Arco will convert its 60 percent working interest in the Sunfish prospect into a sliding-scale, overriding royalty interest on any future production.
No funds exchanged hands in the agreement, Phillips said.
The company said it renamed Sunfish the Tyonek Deep Prospect and plans to drill a delineation well by mid-year.
"This agreement clears the way for that to occur and ensures that ARCO benefits from timely production without additional investments in drilling or infrastructure."

The sliding-scale royalty encourages production by making development of a smaller oil accumulation possible, while ensuring that both companies benefit if the field proves larger than expected, Richter added.

The agreement terminates in 2007 if Phillips fails to find commercial quantities of oil and/or natural gas, the company said. Phillips already owns 100 percent of the shallow production from the North Cook Inlet natural gas unit.
It noted that since 1969 natural gas has been liquefied at the company's liquefied natural gas (LNG) facility on the Kenai Peninsula and shipped to markets in Japan.

The Tyonek Deep negotiations were part of wider talks between the two companies that resulted in separate agreements in which Arco will acquire Phillips' working interest in the Warthog prospect, while Phillips will convert its working interest in West Pt. Thomson into a sliding-scale, overriding royalty interest.
Terms of these agreements were not disclosed, Phillips said. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
